original_value: ABSTRACTThis review examines supply chain risk publications across nine prestigious management, operations, and supply chain journals with respect to exploring trends and emerging topics. Using a refined set of keywords, we extract and filter the most relevant supply chain risk management (SCRM) articles from Scopus between 2001 and 2019. Unlike previous reviews of the SCRM literature, our methodology utilizes both bibliometric and cocitation analyses of publications in selective management and operations and supply chain management journals. In addition to analyzing the current state of the SCRM literature via bibliometric analysis, we delve deeply into the clusters of literature informing SCRM studies through a cocitation analysis. By conducting a text analysis on these clusters, we identify the main themes and provide insights regarding article relevance, theoretical frameworks, and methodologies for each cluster. In addition, we categorize the themes within each cluster into three main groups of matured, developing, and emerging. Based on the identified categories, we provide detailed discussions on the promising avenues for research and practice in three main areas of sustainable SCRM, behavioral SCRM, and nascent methodologies and theories in SCRM studies. Finally, we dedicate a section in our review to discussing the direction of SCRM research during and after the coronavirus disease 2019 era.

result.paraphrase: This review surveys supply chain risk publications in nine leading management, operations, and supply chain journals to identify trends and emerging topics. With a refined keyword set, we retrieve and screen the most relevant supply chain risk management (SCRM) articles from Scopus covering 2001 to 2019. Unlike earlier SCRM literature reviews, our approach combines bibliometric and cocitation analyses across selected management, operations, and supply chain management journals. Beyond mapping the current SCRM literature through bibliometric analysis, we examine in depth the literature clusters that shape SCRM studies via cocitation analysis. Through text analysis of these clusters, we identify the major themes and offer insights into article relevance, theoretical frameworks, and methodologies for each cluster. We also classify the themes in each cluster into three categories: matured, developing, and emerging. Using these categories, we discuss promising research and practice directions in three broad areas: sustainable SCRM, behavioral SCRM, and emerging methodologies and theories in SCRM studies. Finally, we include a section on the direction of SCRM research during and after the coronavirus disease 2019 era.
